easy.q: According to President Oaks, what is the way to overcome our concerns and struggles?
options: Wait for them to go away by themselves
Get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ
Keep them hidden from everyone else
easy.why: President Oaks said that whatever our struggles are, “the way to overcome them is to get closer to our Savior, Jesus Christ.”

easy.q: President Oaks said the Book of Mormon is a great witness that the Lord loves whom?
options: All people, everywhere
Only the people of one land
Mostly people who lived long ago
easy.why: He taught that the Book of Mormon is a great witness “that the Lord loves all people and reaches out to all, everywhere.”

easy.q: In this talk, what did President Oaks say we do each week to renew our covenants?
options: Write in our journals
Pay our fast offerings
Partake of the sacrament
easy.why: President Oaks told us to protect ourselves with the weekly renewing of our covenants “by partaking of the sacrament” and by trying to live those covenants.

easy.q: President Oaks said the Book of Mormon records the Savior’s appearance to which people on the American continent?
options: The Nephites
The Egyptians
The Romans
easy.why: The Book of Mormon records the Savior’s “appearance and teachings to the Nephites on the American continent,” showing that He reaches out to all His flock.

easy.q: At the end of his talk, what did President Oaks call upon all of us to do with the truths he taught?
options: Write them down to study some other year
Act on them and share them with others
Keep them quietly to ourselves at home
easy.why: He called upon all “to act on these truths and to share them with others” so that we may all draw closer to Jesus Christ.

medium.q: President Oaks said strong faith “requires more than strong desire.” What did he say strong faith means?
options: Reaching a point where no questions or doubts remain
Having one great spiritual experience to look back on
Trying daily, one step at a time, with prayer and scripture
Waiting for every answer before taking the next step
medium.why: He taught that strong faith “means daily trying, one step at a time, with prayer and scriptural learning.” Faith grows through steady effort, not desire alone.

medium.q: Speaking of members whose faith in Jesus Christ is diminishing, how did President Oaks describe the Lord’s feelings toward them?
options: He holds back His love until their faith returns
He leaves the seeking to their leaders and families
He stands at a distance until they choose to come back
He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each one
medium.why: President Oaks said, “We love you,” and then, “So does the Lord God! He is relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.” His concern was spoken in love.

medium.q: Why did President Oaks say there is no ultimate conflict between knowledge gained by the scientific method and by the spiritual method?
options: God knows all truth and expects us to learn by both
Science has now confirmed what the scriptures teach
The two methods never deal with the same questions
Spiritual knowledge makes other learning unnecessary
medium.why: He taught there is no ultimate conflict because God, “our omnipotent Eternal Father, knows all truth and expects us to learn by both methods.”

medium.q: President Oaks quoted President Spencer W. Kimball, who defined humility as “teachableness.” In that quotation, what does teachableness help us realize?
options: That we have very little of worth to offer others
That all virtues and abilities are not found in oneself
That the errors of others are usually worse than ours
That learning matters less than simply being obedient
medium.why: President Kimball, as quoted by President Oaks, called teachableness “an ability to realize that all virtues and abilities are not concentrated in one’s self.”

medium.q: President Oaks quoted the Book of Mormon teaching that the Savior “denieth none that come unto him.” What did he use this to show?
options: That all people will be saved whatever they choose
That every nation already has the same scriptures
That His grace is for all, not only a chosen few
That coming unto Him asks nothing further of us
medium.why: He said these teachings “contradict the erroneous assertion that the grace of God saves only a chosen few,” and then declared, “His grace is for all.”

hard.q: The Book of Mormon teaches that the Creator died “for all men.” According to President Oaks, what does this mean for the forgiveness of our sins?
options: Forgiveness comes to everyone without any conditions
We must meet the conditions He has prescribed
Forgiveness is given only to those who never doubt
We earn forgiveness by our works, apart from Him
hard.why: His Atonement is offered to all, but President Oaks taught that “we must comply with the conditions He has prescribed, including faith, repentance, and baptism.” He saves all “if they will hearken unto his voice.”

hard.q: A friend has had a gospel question for months that is still unresolved. Which response best fits what President Oaks taught?
options: Step back from Church activity until the answer comes
Stop thinking about it, since questions show weak faith
Expect that sincere prayer will settle it within days
Hold to the first article of faith and trust the Lord’s timing
hard.why: President Oaks said overcoming doubt “can be a lengthy process.” He counseled us to hold on to the first article of faith and to wait upon the Lord, “trusting in His timing as well as in His promises.”

hard.q: Someone sums up the talk as saying that when science and religion seem to disagree, religion already has the full answer. What did President Oaks say that corrects this?
options: He said such conflicts are settled as soon as we pray with real intent
He said religion’s teachings are sometimes incomplete and science’s are evolving
He said science and religion deal with matters that never truly overlap
He said questions of this kind are best left alone by faithful members
hard.why: He spoke of “the evolving understanding of science and the sometimes incomplete teachings of religion,” and said resolving such conflicts “can be a lengthy process” that involves building faith and strengthening humility.

hard.q: Which statement accurately gives President Oaks’s belief about the inspired teachings the Lord has given His children in various nations?
options: They were given for those nations alone and are meant to remain with them
They will first be given once all nations have received the Book of Mormon
They are already given and will eventually be brought forth to benefit all people
They have already been brought forth in full in the scriptures we now have
hard.why: He said the Lord “will eventually cause the inspired teachings He has given to His children in various nations to be brought forth for the benefit of all people.” They are already given, not yet brought forth, and meant for all.

hard.q: Why did President Oaks recount the Savior’s visit to the Nephites and His words about “other sheep”?
options: To show which ancient people were the most faithful
To show His ministry reached out to all His scattered flock
To show where the events of the Book of Mormon took place
To show why His ministry in Jerusalem had to be so brief
hard.why: President Oaks said the Book of Mormon “adds to our knowledge of how our Savior’s earthly ministry reached out to all of His scattered flock,” supporting the talk’s message that the gospel is for all.
